note: Places a caller asks about often enough to be worth naming. A location is a box and a resolution, not a wind: the atmosphere over it is whatever the caller brings or whatever HRRR says at the hour. radiusMiles has to hold the landform that shapes the wind - a half-mile box in a canyon contains no canyon and the solve has nothing to act on.

locations.name: NRA Whittington Center
locations.note: The coordinate docs/terrain-wind-map.md has used since the first design note. Ground reaches 22.5 degrees at its steepest over a two-mile radius and none of it passes 45, so this solves on layers that follow the ground. Along a 45 degree line from here the terrain does almost nothing - 25 m of relief over two miles - so a line that is meant to cross a canyon needs its own coordinate and probably a larger radius.
